first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it because my grandmother's sapphires will travel from London for the wedding. The first screen is calm and not selling: "Most couples can recite it before they can say where it came from, and few stop to think about what each line asks of them." She summarised it, and I read the heirloom, luxury and travel sections myself.

journey.quote: Then it turns to the choices that matter when the wedding is overseas: which heirloom to wear, what to commission, who to borrow from, and how to carry irreplaceable pieces safely across the world.
journey.reaction: Good. It moves straight to the part that concerns families like mine. No eager tone.

journey.section: 2. Where the rhyme was first printed, and what it means
journey.quote: The rhyme was [first recorded](https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780192829160.001.0001/acref-9780192829160-e-165) in Charlotte Burne's *Shropshire Folk-Lore*, published in 1883, on page 290.
journey.reaction: Page numbers and a reference link. This reads like a librarian, not a planner who simply knows. My assistant skipped it.

journey.section: 3. Something old: heirlooms with a story
journey.quote: Have a jeweller check clasps and settings a few months before the wedding, so nothing gives way on the day.
journey.reaction: Practical and understated. Someone who has seen a clasp go on the day.

journey.section: 3. Something old: heirlooms with a story
journey.quote: You can see the [1841 wedding dress](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O125291/) in the museum's collection.
journey.reaction: Sending me to a museum catalogue for a cotton Sunday-best dress. It doesn't speak to me, and it makes the brand sound like it is researching rather than advising.

journey.section: 3. Something old: heirlooms with a story
journey.quote: Agree with the family before anything is reset.
journey.reaction: Correct. Family pieces are family decisions. That is the discretion I want.

journey.section: 4. Something new: a piece made for the day
journey.quote: Commissioning a piece gives you something new with a reason to exist.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is the register I expect: commission, not purchase.

journey.section: 8. Modern and luxury ways to do all four
journey.quote: A grandmother's sapphire ring, lent for the day, is old, borrowed and blue at once.
journey.reaction: Elegant and exactly my situation. The best line on the page.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: Consider which pieces need to travel at all, and leave anything expensive at home that you can do without.
journey.reaction: Leaving pieces at home isn't the answer for me. I want to know who escorts them, how they're secured at the venue and who holds them between events.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: Credit card travel insurance may only cover the cardholder, and generally only the trip paid for on the card.
journey.reaction: Credit card insurance and per-item limits. This is written for a standard package client. Nothing about secure transport, specialist cover or working with our own security.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments around the day, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: One contact is right. Still nothing that tells me they handle 300 guests, exclusive use or security.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and your advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quiet and professional. No 'from' price, no discount talk. Inclusions sounds slightly like a package, but acceptable.

unanswered_questions: Can they arrange secure, escorted transport for valuable family jewellery to the venue, and hold it securely between events?
Can they work with our own security team and our insurers or jewellers?
Have they delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests with exclusive use of the property?
How is privacy protected: vendor NDAs, photography and social media rules for guests?
Can they coordinate a commission with a jeweller of our choosing across several countries?
Is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: The rhyme was [first recorded](https://www.oxfordreference.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780192829160.001.0001/acref-9780192829160-e-165) in Charlotte Burne's *Shropshire Folk-Lore*, published in 1883, on page 290.
turn_offs_found.why: Citations, page numbers and catalogue links make the brand sound like a researcher. An authority simply states it.

turn_offs_found.quote: As at November 2026, the Australian Government's [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/while-overseas/protecting-yourself-crime/theft-and-robbery) advice gives a clear basis for planning.
turn_offs_found.why: Leaning on government consumer advice signals the brand is borrowing authority rather than having it, and pitches the section at a standard traveller.

turn_offs_found.quote: Credit card travel insurance may only cover the cardholder, and generally only the trip paid for on the card.
turn_offs_found.why: Budget-traveller detail tells me I'm being treated like a standard package client.

would_share_with: My assistant, to add jewellery security and escort questions to the planner shortlist
My mother, for the 'one piece, several lines' idea with my grandmother's sapphires

cta_reaction.why: Understated, fee agreed in writing, no package talk. But I don't fill in web forms and nothing shows they've handled my scale or security. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Remove the visible sourcing in body copy (Oxford Reference link, page number, V&A dress link, 'As at November 2026, the Australian Government's Smartraveller advice') so the voice states facts with authority rather than citing them.

Rebalance section 9 away from consumer insurance detail (credit card cover, 'leave anything expensive at home') towards how a planner handles irreplaceable pieces: secure transport, safekeeping at the venue, coordination with the family's own security and insurers, if true.

Add one understated line in section 8 or 9 showing the brand handles large family weddings with exclusive use and private logistics, if true, and offer a private conversation rather than only a web form.
